newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Optus to spend A$50 mln on ATMs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Optus to spend A$50 mln on ATMs.

text.p: Australia's second largest telecommunications company, Optus Communications Pty Ltd, said on Monday it planned to invest A$50 million to upgrade its ATM (Asynchronous Transfer Mode) network, enabling phone customers to have access to the Internet.
Optus said as part of the investment it had signed a five supply agreement with Canadian-based Newbridge Networks Corp for the supply of ATM and frame relay equipment.
The rollout of the ATM network over the five years means that Newbridge will invest an estimated A$10.7 million in the Australian market, Optus said.

Optus said the ATM technology will be deployed in its Sydney and Melbourne networks from October this year and will be extended to Adelaide around December and then to Canberra, Brisbane and Perth in the first half of 1997.
Newbridge is a manufacturer of telecommunications network products and systems.
Optus said it had already committed A$30 million to the project and the A$50 million would be in addition to the funds already invested.
"Optus' new ATM backbone network is an investment which will pay dividends in allowing Optus to maximise use of its existing networks," it said.
